note: The one registry for every cascade bound the spec leaves open, plus the settled bounds a cascade gate reads. A bound with a value must name its unit, the gate it feeds, its owning ticket, its source and the date the value was taken; a bound without one stays OPEN and require_bound() raises by name. The four frozen reply/cut budgets are read from the budget record and must never carry a literal here. Ticket 04 fills OPEN entries with value + source + date; that is a data edit, not a code edit.

budget_record.note: Frozen demo-scoreboard budget record (freeze-guard commit 835a5f1e). Read at load; never copied.

reply_gap.p50_ms.note: Median reply gap. Consumers: the reply-gap gate, the kill criterion (ticket 119).

reply_gap.p95_ms.note: Tail reply gap. A small-sample scope is judged against this, never its own median (ticket 119).

barge_in.real_cut_ms.note: Audio must stop within this of caller speech start.

barge_in.filler_resume_tail_ms.note: The unheard tail resumes within this.

budget.route_managed_ratio.source: spec: settled money policy — the daily counter routes new calls to managed at 80% of the cap
budget.route_managed_ratio.note: A live cascade call is untouched; only the next new call moves.

budget.refuse_cascade_ratio.source: spec: settled money policy — refuse cascade at 100% of the cap, never the call
budget.refuse_cascade_ratio.note: Refusing cascade is a routing decision, not a fallback event.

breaker.probe_interval_ms.source: spec: M1 state transitions — a probe is due at least 30 s after the last probe, and three probe successes each at least 30 s apart close the leg
breaker.probe_interval_ms.note: One number for both rules: the due interval and the minimum spacing between counted successes. Staleness is 2x this. Breaker.from_registry() reads it; the breaker never defaults one.

stt.handshake_ms.source: spec: Meta STT handshake — the first JSON text frame within 10 s of connecting
stt.handshake_ms.note: No acknowledgement inside this fails the call visibly and records the reason.

stt.session_max_ms.source: spec: Meta STT session limits — a realtime session runs up to 60 minutes and has no resume token
stt.session_max_ms.note: Vendor limit, not a tunable. The adapter reconnects before it at a turn boundary; the bounded handshake is the margin, so no second number is invented.

tts.idle_timeout_ms.source: spec: the TTS session closes after 120 s with no frame in either direction
tts.idle_timeout_ms.note: The keepalive interval must sit strictly below this and inside the control-frame budget.

tts.generate_char_cap.source: spec: a long sentence is split under the 2,000-character Generate cap; an over-cap Generate closes with 3006
tts.generate_char_cap.note: Flushing per token is forbidden; this is the sentence ceiling.

tts.audio_loss_tolerance_ms.source: spec: FlushDone.audio_duration_ms is compared with the bytes received and a difference beyond a few milliseconds fails the call as audio loss; 5 ms covers the vendor's whole-millisecond report rounding (at most 1 ms) and leaves every real dropped frame visible
tts.audio_loss_tolerance_ms.note: One 24 kHz 16-bit audio frame is normally 10-20 ms, so a lost frame is far outside this bound. Not to be restated in code.

probe.model_max_completion_tokens.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. the spec bounds the model probe ('one minimal completion with max_completion_tokens small enough to bound cost') but states no number. A probe without a cap is not a probe, so the probe refuses to run until this is recorded. Synthesis costs nothing here: the voice probe sends an empty Generate (0 characters, inside tts.generate_char_cap).
probe.model_max_completion_tokens.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): a breaker probe must cost a negligible number of tokens

budget.daily_cap.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 5. The 80%/100% behavior is fixed; this value is not.
budget.daily_cap.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): USD/day, roughly 8x a 100-call day at current rates; revisit after a week of volume

budget.per_call_ceiling.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 6. The drain behavior is fixed; this value is not.
budget.per_call_ceiling.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): USD/call, well above a 5-minute cascade call at v1 rates

deploy.drain_max_wait_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 7. A live call is never terminated by the drain; this is the operational wait.
deploy.drain_max_wait_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): a live call is never killed; this is the operational wait

turn.stall_guard_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 8. Closes an abandoned turn with no reply; the later turn is still answered.
turn.stall_guard_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): the existing p95 reply budget, not a new number

tool.loop_cap.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 9. Until supplied the loop is bounded by the turn budget and the stall guard.
tool.loop_cap.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): three tool rounds, then the turn fails visibly

tts.keepalive_interval_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. the spec fixes the behavior (named interval below the idle timeout) but not the interval.
tts.keepalive_interval_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): below the vendor 120 s idle close

budget.day_boundary.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 16. UTC is assumed, not yet confirmed.
budget.day_boundary.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): UTC, confirming the spec assumption

ci.browser_e2e_budget_s.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. spec open dependency 18. Over budget, the job moves to a required pre-merge job, never nightly-only.
ci.browser_e2e_budget_s.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): current run ~8.5 s; 120 s leaves CI headroom

turn.reply_task_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. the reply task is bounded; the spec does not state the bound.
turn.reply_task_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): a whole reply task is bounded; no hang

tool.timeout_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. the tool hop is bounded and a timeout becomes a failed tool result.
tool.timeout_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): the tool hop is off the latency-critical path

reconnect.handshake_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. a reconnect handshake is bounded; the STT first-frame ack uses stt.handshake_ms.
reconnect.handshake_ms.source: spec: Meta STT first-frame ack within 10 s; owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04) for reuse on reconnect

envelope.ttl_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. the spec fixes the behaviour (the signed body envelope is short-lived and an expired one is refused at the service before any vendor socket) but states no number. A body is never signed with an invented TTL: envelope.sign_body refuses until ticket 04 records value + source + date.
envelope.ttl_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): short-lived signed body envelope, refused after expiry

call_token.ttl_ms.note: SUPPLIED by ticket 04. The call token is its own signed material with its own short window; it does not borrow envelope.ttl_ms, so retuning one never moves the other.
call_token.ttl_ms.source: owner decision 2026-10-30 (ticket 04): short-lived call token, refused after expiry at connect

playout.cushion_ms.source: voni/public/playout-processor.js TARGET_CUSHION_S = 0.5; recorded by ticket 04 on 2026-10-30
playout.cushion_ms.note: The configured target cushion, included in the perceived reply gap; not measured from a live buffer.
